correctness.rationale: For n=2^s-1, the path characteristic continuant f_{2m+1}=z f_m² gives f_n=z^n, while e_1 is cyclic, yielding exactly one nilpotent path block. The clique adjacency I+H_q splits into 0 plus identity on zero-sum vectors for q odd, or identity plus a rank-one square-zero Jordan J_2 for q even. In F_2[x,y]/(x^n,y²), multiplication by x+y has ranks 2(n-t) for 0<=t<n, rank 1 at t=n and 0 at n+1, proving its two Jordan blocks have lengths n+1,n-1. The resulting full Jordan forms imply all fixed-space, entry-depth and orbit formulas. Direct edge-defined adjacency computations validated matrix rank profiles, four exhaustive small full-state cases, and adjacent-length invertibility; these are supplementary finite tests, not infinite proofs.

Nevertheless a more general unlocated theory of characteristic-two Jordan sums could imply parts of the calculation, so uniqueness is not asserted.

value.rationale: Across all dyadic-minus-one path lengths and all clique widths, each even width and its successor odd width have identical fixed-state counts and primitive orbit counts at every period yet opposite state-space behaviour: complete immediate recurrence versus recurrent fraction 2^-n and half the states requiring n updates. The precise Jordan forms explain this genuinely structural orbit/transient invisibility, while changing the number of path columns to 4^r at n=4^r-1 creates a sharp natural reversible boundary. This is an infinite two-parameter dynamical classification, not an arbitrary isolated case or routine restatement of path nilpotence.
